when generating the `hashCode` of an element, we do use the size returned by `__iterate`. But in case of `Ordered` element, the internal representation of the underlying list might contain undefined elements :

Example:

const m \= OrderedMap({a:'a', b:'b'}).remove('a')

m.size is 1, the `__iterate` function will iterate only one time on the `b` key, but the internal `_list` element, will have two elements: `[undefined, ['b', 'b']]`:

[![image](https://private-user-images.githubusercontent.com/1398469/350908574-ec4736a0-fbfd-4ae0-b860-6eccbb1e54a5.png?jwt=eyJ0eXAiOiJKV1QiLCJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9..thdBrmqh0no-AvTihuCwcCUjTvedHrPRh1i9OMPZVN4)](https://private-user-images.githubusercontent.com/1398469/350908574-ec4736a0-fbfd-4ae0-b860-6eccbb1e54a5.png?jwt=eyJ0eXAiOiJKV1QiLCJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9..thdBrmqh0no-AvTihuCwcCUjTvedHrPRh1i9OMPZVN4)  
See [https://runkit.com/jdeniau/immutable-hashcode-using-internal-list-size](https://runkit.com/jdeniau/immutable-hashcode-using-internal-list-size)

I think that we should not use the value returned by `__iterate`, and use the object size directly.

**Fix**: In `src/predicates/isValueObject.js`, the `Hasher.hashCollection` method was seeding the final murmur hash mix with the value returned by `collection.__iterate()`. For `OrderedMap`/`OrderedSet`, the internal `_list` retains holes (`undefined` entries) when a non-last element is removed, so `__iterate` returns the stale list size rather than the actual number of entries — causing equal collections to produce different `hashCode()` values. The fix uses `collection.size` instead (src/predicates/isValueObject.js:53), which also makes `deepEqual`-based equality consistent since equal objects now share hash codes.
